section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Midrashic statement about the primary Shechinah being in the lower realms contains two concepts: the superiority of the lower realms and the unique level of that Shechinah, which is clarified through the idea that G-d desired the dwelling to be made specifically through the work of lower beings, particularly through the service of subjugation and transformation.
section.t: And one can explain the elucidation of this,
that in the statement of the Midrash, "The primary Shechinah was in the lower realms,"
there are two matters.
The superiority of the lower realms
(relative to the upper realms),
that specifically in them was the primary Shechinah,
and that the level of the Shechinah that was in the lower realms is
(not merely Shechinah,
but rather)
the primary Shechinah.
And the matters in the maamar
(in the first chapter)
are an explanation of these two matters.
For this, that He desired that the revelation of G-dliness below
(a dwelling place in the lower realms)
should be through the service of man, emphasizes the superiority of the lower realms.
For in addition to this, that He desired that the dwelling
(the revelation of G-dliness)
be in the lower realms,
He desired that also the making of the dwelling be through the service of the lower realms.
For through the fact that the revelation of G-dliness in the lower realms is drawn down through their service,
they become vessels for the revelation,
and moreover,
that the revelation drawn down in them is from the aspect of the lower realms themselves.
And it adds,
that the service through which the dwelling is made is the service of subjugation and transformation,
for through this it is even more emphasized that the revelation drawn down in the lower realms is from their own aspect.
For in addition to this, that the revelation drawn down in them is through their service,
also the service
(through which the revelation is drawn down)
is a service that is from the aspect of the lower realms.

And this, that the drawing down through the service of subjugation and transformation is a drawing down of the light that is equal in all worlds, is an explanation of the phrase "the primary Shechinah in the lower realms,"
and as explained elsewhere21
that the primary Shechinah is the light that is above worlds.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two concepts are also understood from the Sages' language of "desire," which is above reason and stems from the Essence (Atzmus), indicating that the dwelling in the lower realms is for the revelation of the Essence itself.
section.t: And to add,
that the two aforementioned matters are also understood from the language of our Sages, of blessed memory,16
"He desired... a dwelling place in the lower realms,"
specifically "He desired."
And the explanation is,
that in the Zohar and in Etz Chaim it is stated,
that there are reasons for the creation of the worlds
[for in the Zohar22
it is stated that the reason is "so that they may know Him," and in Etz Chaim23
it is stated that the reason is "in order to reveal the perfection of His powers and actions"],

and in the aforementioned statement of our Sages it is stated that the creation of the worlds was because the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place for Himself in the lower realms,
for the matter of "desire" is above reason,
and in the language of the Alter Rebbe24
"Upon a desire, there is no question,"
meaning that the matter of desire is in a place
(level)
where a question does not apply, because it is above intellect.
And the explanation of this is known,
that the Zohar and Etz Chaim speak about the matter of the creation of the worlds as it is from the aspect of revelations,
and since revelations, even the most sublime revelations, are defined by some definition,
the will to do something is because that thing is in accordance with their definition
(reason),
and in the aforementioned statement of our Sages, it speaks about the matter of creation that is from the aspect of the Essence (Atzmus),
for since it is not defined by any definition,
the will for the creation of the worlds in the Essence is not because there is some superiority in the creation, but rather because He so desired,
above reason.
And just as the matter of "desire" is in the Essence,
so too the matter that He desires is that He have a dwelling place in the lower realms,
for the matter of a dwelling place is25
like a person's dwelling, where the essence of the person dwells in the dwelling,
meaning that in the lower realms there will be the drawing down and revelation of the Essence (Atzmus).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section proves that the purpose of creation is the desire for a dwelling in the lowest world, because the reasons of "knowing Him" and "revealing His powers" would have been fulfilled by the higher worlds alone, and the existence of the lower worlds, which lack inherent advantage, demonstrates that the intent is for the Essence itself.
section.t: And it is known26
that the proof that the cause for the creation of the worlds is because He desired
(above reason),
is,
that in order for the matter of "so that they may know Him"
(knowledge of G-dliness)
to exist, it would have been sufficient to create the upper worlds
(the World of Atzilus and the worlds of Ein Sof that are above Atzilus)
and there would have been no need for the creation of the lower worlds.
And on the contrary,
the primary matter of "so that they may know Him" is specifically in the upper worlds.
For the knowledge and comprehension of G-dliness in the lower worlds
(the spiritual worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah)
is only of the existence of G-dliness and not of its essence.
And all the more so in the physical World of Asiyah, where even the existence of G-dliness is not felt.
And similarly regarding the reason of "to reveal the perfection of His powers and actions,"
that in order to reveal the perfection of His powers, it would have been sufficient to create the upper worlds,
for since even the upper worlds are a creation and their coming into existence is through the way of renewal
(yesh mei'ayin),
therefore, through the Ein Sof bringing them into existence, the power within Him is revealed27
(that He has the power to bring into existence something new)28.
And furthermore, one could say,
that the primary revelation of the perfection of His powers is specifically in the creation of the upper worlds.
For since the creation of the lower worlds
(Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah)
is through the G-dly power that brings them into existence being concealed from them,
behold, in this action of the power
(the creation of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah),
the power is not revealed.
And all the more so it is not revealed in the creation of this lowest world,
where the concealment of the creative power is even greater.
And from the fact that
(also)
the spiritual worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah were created,
and all the more so from the creation of this physical world,
which has no
(in itself)
advantage,
and in the language of the Alter Rebbe29
"the lowest realm, beneath which there is no lower realm,"
it is proven,
that the ultimate purpose of creation is
(not from the aspect of reason,
but rather)
because He so desired that this lowest world be a dwelling place for Him,
for His Essence (Atzmus).
